tasks.registered_metrics_text:
a) Define the metric(s) to assess a property of an algorithm. These metrics should reflect the desired algorithm
properties described in assessment aim(s) (see above). State which metric(s) were used to compute the ranking(s) (if
any).
  • Example 1: Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC)
  • Example 2: Area under curve (AUC)
Macro-averaged F1-score and Kappa coefficient

b) Justify why the metric(s) was/were chosen, preferably with reference to the biomedical application.

1) F1-score takes both recall and precision into consideration, which is calculated as:
F1-score = (2*recall*precision) / (recall+precision)


 Liver Lesion Diagnosis Challenge on Multi-phase MRI

2) Cohen’s kappa, a quantitative measure of the reliability for two raters evaluating the same thing, is calculated as
follows:
Kappa coefficient = (Po-Pe) / (1-Pe)
where Po is the observed relative agreement between raters and Pe is the hypothetical probability of agreement
by chance.
tasks.registered_ranking_text:
a) Describe the method used to compute a performance rank for all submitted algorithms based on the generated
metric results on the test cases. Typically the text will describe how results obtained per case and metric are aggregated
to arrive at a final score/ranking.

1) Calculate Cohen's Kappa coefficient.
2) Calculate the F1-score for each lesion type, and then calculate the macro-average of F1-score (m-F1) for all
lesion types.
3) Rank the average score of m-F1 and Cohen's Kappa coefficient as the final task score.
4) Tie if the scores are equal.

b) Describe the method(s) used to manage submissions with missing results on test cases.

If an algorithm fails to generate an outcome metric for a particular test case, we will penalize the final results to
ensure fairness. To be more specific, a penalty value will be subtracted from the evaluation score, and its
calculation formula is as follows: evaluation score * [(number of missing cases * 4) / ( total number of test cases)].

c) Justify why the described ranking scheme(s) was/were used.

Calculating the average of the two metrics can reflect the performance of the algorithm more comprehensively
and avoid the problem that the algorithm performs well on one metric but poorly on others. Specifically, for any
lesion type, the F1-score is computed from the confusion matrix, which maintains a balance between precision
and recall to handle uneven class distribution. The Cohen's Kappa coefficient can reflect the consistency between
predicted and real results, which can handle unbalanced classification distribution.

registered_task_submissions.protocol_description: 1) GitHub Repository: data download links will be available in our GitHub repository, and we will also provide a code repository comprising data processing and loading, model training and evaluation, prediction, and etc. Meanwhile, a baseline model will also be provided for reference. More details can be found at https://github.com/LMMMEng/LLD-MMRI2023. 2) Data Release Stage: The training set, validation set, and test set will be released sequentially in three stages. First, the training dataset (with annotations) and the validation dataset (without annotations) will be released on April 28th. Second, annotations on the validation set will be accessible on July 8th. Third, the test dataset (without annotations) will be released on August 2nd. That is, participants will be provided with annotated training and validation datasets as well as non-annotated test data before the final evaluation. 3) Algorithm Development Stage: participants need to design and output a satisfactory model based on the released datasets and annotations on their own computing devices. When the validations/test sets are released, a prediction code will be provided to generate the prediction score for each case from the test set for reference. It should be noted that participants must generate prediction results in strict accordance with our pre-defined file format (case id with predictions for each category). 4) Algorithm Evaluation Stage: participants are required to submit their predictions on the test set within a specified time frame. We will then calculate performance metrics (Macro-averaged F1-score and Cohen's Kappa coefficient) of their algorithms based on their submissions and ground-truth annotations. The challenge consists of four evaluation stages. In the first three stages, the ranking will be updated based on the predicted results of the algorithm on the validation set. Participants will have a 24-hour submission window on May 26th, June 16th, and July 7th to submit their prediction results. On July 8th, annotations on the validation set will be released to further support model design and training. In the final stage, the test set (without annotations) will be released on August 2nd. Participants are required to submit their predictions on August 4th, and the predicted results at this stage will determine the final ranking. Regarding the submission method, participants should send their prediction files to the official email address specified on GitHub within a specified period after completing predictions. Note that if a team commits multiple times within a single submission window, we will only use the last successful commit. Then, the algorithm performance will be shown based on the submitted results and ground-truth annotations of the test set. 5) Result Display Stage: We will sort out the effective results in a short time and display the scores and rankings of each team on GitHub. 6) Verification Stage: To ensure the fairness of the challenge, the top-10 teams will be required to disclose their codes and model weights on GitHub or other publicly accessible websites for verification. We will use these codes and model weights to verify that the reproduced results are consistent with the submitted predictions. If teams fail to disclose their codes and model weights within the stipulated time frame, they will be removed from the leaderboard. If serious discrepancies are detected using disclosed codes and model weights, we will notify the corresponding teams to take remedial actions. If they fail to complete within the allotted time, they will be Liver Lesion Diagnosis Challenge on Multi-phase MRI removed from the leaderboard and the leaderboard will be adjusted accordingly. New teams that subsequently enter the top-10 will also be required to comply with the same rules. More detailed submission instructions will be given at https://github.com/LMMMEng/LLC-3DAM-MRI2023.
